title: SDK ops mini-lab — distilled templates and runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, copy-friendly internal lab and ops template set for onboarding engineers and SEs to the Redwood SDK quickly. Focus is on reproducible mini-labs (15–60 minutes) that teach the common production touchpoints: auth, instrumented requests, failure rehearsal, and light performance checks.

Audience:
- New developer-experience hires (first 2 weeks)
- Solutions engineers running customer workshops
- Engineers wanting a fast, reproducible baseline for embedding the Redwood SDK into demo apps

What this file is: distilled recipes, CLI snippets, telemetry templates, and a short runbook for the five canonical mini-labs we use in internal demos. Keep these intentionally terse so they can be copy-pasted into workshop docs, Slack replies, or a hands-on script.

Mini-lab 1 — Hello-instrumented: quick auth + telemetry (10–15m)
Goal: Get an authenticated SDK call sending minimal telemetry to our dev pipeline.
Steps:
- Preconditions: developer has API key in env (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and Python installed.
- Copy/paste snippet (python):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  import os
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = c.text.generate(prompt='Say hello to telemetry', telemetry={'lab': 'hello-instrumented', 'user_id': 'se-demo'})
  print(resp.text)
- Expected telemetry events: request.start, request.finish, token.count.
- Quick verification: open telemetry dashboard -> filter by lab=hello-instrumented; confirm a single request.start/finish pair within 30s.
Failure notes:
- If nothing appears: confirm API key scope and local clock skew (telemetry ingestion drops >2m skew).
- If token.count missing: ensure SDK version >= 1.6.2.

Mini-lab 2 — Prefix-caching smoke (15–25m)
Goal: Demonstrate prefix/KV cache improving p99 latency for repeated prompts.
Recipe:
- Small Node snippet (shell-ready):
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
  node -e "const R=require('redwood'); const c=new R.Client({apiKey:process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); async function run(){for(let i=0;i<6;i++){const r=await c.text.generate({prompt:'Rewrite: The quick brown fox',cache:{enabled:true,cache_key:'fox-demo'}}); console.log(i,r.timing.latency_ms);} } run()"
- Observe latencies: first call higher, subsequent fall.
- Metric to capture: trace.span:inference.duration and trace.cache.hit_rate.
Pitfalls:
- If no cache hit: confirm model variant supports prefix caching (see model catalog).

Mini-lab 3 — Canary fallback simulation (20–40m)
Goal: Show rollback/failover by toggling a canary route and verifying automatic fallback to a baseline model.
Checklist:
- Admin UI: create route 'labs/canary-demo' pointing to model v2-canary with fallback to v1-stable.
- Simulate degraded canary: in the console set canary instance drain=1 or add a temporary capacity annotation.
- Send traffic (curl):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"route":"labs/canary-demo","prompt":"summarize: quick note"}'
- Observe: requests are served; fallback events recorded in rollout logs.
Verification points:
- See rollout.log entries: fallback.reason=capacity and fallback.target=v1-stable
- Latency: fallback may increase median by ~15–40ms depending on model.

Mini-lab 4 — Quality regression smoke test (30–60m)
Goal: Run a small set of golden prompts against two model versions and push a regression alert if BLEU/ROUGE drops beyond threshold.
Toolkit:
- small prompts list (provided below)
- local eval harness (python script included in /sdk-samples/evals)
Procedure:
- Run: python evals/run_eval.py --route labs/regression --baseline v1-stable --candidate v2-canary
- Thresholds: rouge-l >= 0.86, exact-match >= 0.74 for this tiny suite
- On failure: open ticket JIRA-DEVEXP-REG and attach eval output JSON.
Quick tips:
- Use smaller prompt timeouts (3s) during canary to get fast feedback; increase then for final checks.

Mini-lab 5 — Billing-aware batching and cost-check (15–30m)
Goal: Illustrate the cost impact of different batching strategies and token limits.
Steps:
- Two quick configs: continuous batching enabled, batch_size=8 vs batch_size=1
- Send identical 100 short prompts and measure total billing tokens reported in cost api: /billing/usage?sandbox=true
- Expect: batch_size=8 should show ~10–30% token-efficiency improvement depending on prompt prefix repeat rate.

Common telemetry templates (copy/paste)
- request.start payload: "{"event":"request.start","route":"labs/<lab-name>","model":"<model-id>","lab":"<lab-name>","user_id":"<id>"}"
- request.finish payload: "{"event":"request.finish","latency_ms":<n>,"tokens":<n>,"cache_hit":true|false}"
- rollout.log: "canary_id=<id> event=drain reason=manual target=v1-stable"

Short runbook (for SEs delivering a 30min workshop)
- 0–5m: Set expectations, confirm everyone has REDWOOD_API_KEY and git clone sdk-samples repo.
- 5–20m: Run Mini-labs 1 & 2 together; ask participants to copy telemetry dashboard link.
- 20–35m: Canary demo (lab 3) — execute a controlled failover and have attendees observe rollout logs.
- 35–50m: Run quick eval (lab 4) and discuss regression alerts.
- 50–60m: Discuss cost tradeoffs and show billing dashboard differences from lab 5.

Templates for workshop slides (short bullets):
- Slide: "Why instrument SDK calls?" -> low friction rollout, debug by correlating client traces to model traces.
- Slide: "Cache and batching tradeoffs" -> p99 vs unit cost; when to prefer each.
- Slide: "Rollouts and fallbacks" -> safe canaries reduce blast radius.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Add a one-click workbook that pre-populates telemetry filters for each lab (follow-on work).
- Investigate a smaller local eval harness with prebuilt thresholds (customer-facing).
- Confirm exact telemetry field names with Observability team (Leah, Ravi).

Appendix — short prompts (copyable)
- Summarize: "Describe the main benefit of prefix caching in one sentence."
- Paraphrase: "Rewrite: Please trim the email to be polite and under 60 words."
- QA: "Given the snippet, what is the likely bug?"

Where to copy from and next steps:
- Move polished templates to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-LABS once validated.
- Follow up PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples (add mini-lab runner) — target: Miguel.

If you use these in a customer-facing workshop, mark the session notes in JIRA and attach the telemetry query outputs.

Signed,
Asha

(Short changelog)
2025-07-12: initial sketch.
2025-08-01: added canary checklist and telemetry payload examples.
